analysis.title: GS McGeoch - GS Materials Oct 26: Brazil call at 11:15 UKT, GALP cancels Moeve, NHY d/g, TECK strike, RIO's RSI of 20, ENR into CMD
key_insights: Brazil election: Lula won. BRL is trading 12% lower, EWZ is indicating 18% lower, and the Japan-listed IBOV ETF is down 15%, limit down. The desk's obvious pair to watch is VALE.US vs PBR.US, and it believes everyone is long PBR.

Iron ore price is the bigger watch for near-term VALE sentiment. At the GS conference the VALE CEO said 10% or 160mt of supply is at risk at spot prices, with 15mt already cut. He is bullish on China steel resilience, Vietnam (25 to 100mt) and India (175 to 600mt), and sees only 5mt at risk for VALE.
14-day RSI on US-listed iron ore names: RIO US 20, RIO LN 21, BHP 26, VALE 30. The desk reads this as the market's verdict on RIO's strategy and delivery.

RIO's asset sale programme started in a sellers market in 4Q25 and has since turned into a buyers market, while the cost to execute rose with rates. RIO has also cut costs. The CEO's timeline for the sales is 'by YE'. The desk says RIO needs a win and needs investors rather than traders, and that peers are moving faster. It understands the tactical cover.
TECK: a strike began at HVC in BC, the first in 35 years, after the 5-year collective agreement expired on Sept 30. TECK reports on 29/10.

Copper supply is the key. The 2027 benchmark TC (treatment charge) is a big ask. China smelter utilisation is trending toward the low 70% range. One speaker at the GS conference suggested refined metal output could fall 3%/2%/2% over the next 3 quarters. The desk says supply-driven moves are exponential and demand-driven moves are linear.

GALP: the stock starts -5% and the desk (Trading, Pete) says it should become a default funding short given the 4Q freight impact and the cancelled Moeve catalyst. The Moeve deal is off, and it was a main reason investors were long, since it would have allowed more leverage in subsidiaries and more cash returned. Results were fine: EBITDA/EBIT 3%/1.5% above consensus, adj CFFO ex WC 1.2bn about $200m better than VA. Guidance was slightly weak: CF guidance was raised to 3.9bn, which implies weaker 4Q realisations (the sensitivities implied more than 4bn).

NHY: GIR downgraded to neutral after last Friday's results. Headwinds are higher 2027 unhedged gas prices, premiums normalising faster than expected, new regional supply (Indonesia in particular) and no clear near-term catalyst. 2026/27 EBITDA is cut 6%/6%, 2028 is raised 4% on cost revisions. The 12m price target is cut 21% to NOK 79/sh, based on a 50/50 blend (from 25/75) of 1x NAV and 5.5x EV/EBITDA (from 6.5x). NHY hosts a CMD on Nov 25.

Siemens Energy: CMD on 11 Nov. GIR rates it Buy on the Conviction List. New 2030 targets are expected, with GSe about 11% above BBG consensus 2030 EBITA, and a potential €30bn capital return through 2030.

NEM.US: team reiterates Buy after results. Q3 was +5% q/q and +19% y/y on improved margins, with in-line production. Ex by-products, unit AISC was up about 3% QoQ. It bought back $1.9bn with $2.8bn still authorised. CY27 guidance is in line with GS: production +4%, unit costs +8-10%, capex $3.85bn, slightly above GS.

China A-shares midday: weaker early on a surge in oil and ahead of megacap tech earnings, then rebounded into the morning close on expected national team support, which has been quiet so far. Optical module names are under pressure ahead of earnings from Innolight, Eoptolink and TFC. Cambricon was resilient after earnings despite a sales miss on raw material constraints. Precious metals led the underperformance, with Zijin Mining down as much as 7% after earnings. Defensives (liquor, financials, healthcare) were bid, and about 3000 stocks traded lower.

earnings_insights: GALP 3Q: EBITDA 3% and EBIT 1.5% above consensus (reported vs consensus). Adj CFFO ex WC was 1.2bn, about $200m better than VA. CF guidance was raised to 3.9bn, which implies weaker 4Q realisations.
NEM Q3 (reported): +5% q/q and +19% y/y on improved margins. Production was in line. CY27 guidance: production +4%, unit costs +8-10%, capex $3.85bn, slightly above GS.
Zijin Mining fell as much as 7% after earnings (reported).
Cambricon reported a sales miss on raw material constraints, with a higher inventory and positive guidance.
Upcoming CMDs: Siemens Energy on 11 Nov, NHY on 25 Nov.

tension_points.bull_case: RIO has considerable interest, its assets are world class and command a premium, and the CEO targets completing sales by year-end. Announced Q3 deals were not in analyst numbers.
tension_points.bear_case: The market is a buyers market, execution costs rose with rates, and peers are moving faster. RIO's RSI of 20 shows weak sentiment on delivery.
tension_points.what_invalidates: No asset sale announced by year-end, the CEO's stated timeline.
